title: automat operator determinations
description: The operator's own assertions about an assessment — the mechanism that makes docs/assessment-reporting.md's Invariant 2 enforceable. Without this file, a satisfied/MET value would have to be typed directly into a generated document, which is exactly the signable-artifact shape Invariant 1 forbids. As a file it is reviewable, diffable, and content-hashed into the evidence chain like a catalog, so a later reader can tell which human assertions were in force when a report was generated and no assertion can be revised after the fact without the hash moving.
$comment: CONTENT HASH SCOPE: content_sha256 (recorded out-of-band, in the evidence manifest record and in assessment-result-v1's `determinations` field — there is no self-referential hash field in this document, the same convention every other document in schema/ follows) covers every field EXCEPT schema_version, for the same reason given on every other profile's $comment: a major version bump changes what the covered fields mean, and a reader that does not understand the version refuses the document before any hash is consulted.

revision_determination.description: Required when the obligation profile being assessed leaves its control-catalog revision unpinned (control_catalogs[].revision_policy: operator-determined — NIH's controlled-access data expectations are the shipped case). automat ships NO default: 'most institutions use rN' is not a default and not a hint, because a default here would silently pick an institution's compliance posture for it. `assess` refuses to run under such a profile without this field rather than proceeding without one.

determinations.description: The operator's own claims, one per objective or group of objectives satisfied together. Every value here is a human assertion the operator is choosing to make and sign for — never a value automat wrote for them; see docs/assessment-reporting.md Invariant 2.

prose.description: Single-line human text. Control characters are rejected because these strings are rendered into reports and tables, where a newline forges a row.

long_prose.description: Multi-line human text. Newlines and tabs are permitted; other control characters are not.

round_trip_id.description: An id an operator types into this file by hand and may later need to type back on a command line or read off a printed report. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore only — the same class automat's own round-trip fields use (CLAUDE.md rule 8) — so a value carrying a quote or a space cannot misdirect a shell or defeat a double-click selection.

determination.description: One determination: a value from the profile's own vocabulary, who is asserting it and when, and the objective(s) it covers.

id.description: This determination's own identifier within the file — what assessment-result-v1's per-objective `determination` field points back to. Round-trip: an operator reviewing a rendered result may need to find this exact entry again in the source file.

objectives.description: The control or objective id(s) this determination satisfies, e.g. ['AC.L1-b.1.i']. More than one when a single assertion covers a group deliberately treated as one practice.

value.description: The determination value, spelled exactly as the obligation profile's determinations.values names it (e.g. 'MET', 'NOT MET'). automat validates this against the named profile's vocabulary at load time; a value the profile does not define is refused rather than silently accepted.

statement.description: The basis for this determination, in the operator's own words — the same reasoning docs/assessment-reporting.md's attestation model gives for requiring a statement rather than a bare value: a reader evaluates a sentence, not a tick.

responsible_party.description: Who is making this determination, by name or role. Not decoration: it is what makes an assertion attributable, and an assessment where every determination names the same person who also ran the tool is a fact a reviewer should be able to see.

revision_determination.description: The operator's own declared revision for a control catalog whose obligation profile leaves it unpinned, recorded with who determined it and when — hashed into the evidence chain like any other determination in this file, so a later reader can tell which revision was in force without needing anything outside this document.

catalog.description: The catalog family this determination pins a revision for, matching an obligation profile's control_catalogs[].catalog value, e.g. 'nist-sp-800-171'.

revision.description: The revision the operator has determined applies, as they would cite it (e.g. 'Revision 2').

statement.description: Why this revision, in the operator's own words — the institution's own reading of an ambiguous instrument, not automat's.
